name: Macaroni Bashamel
description: Macaroni Béchamel is the ultimate Egyptian soul food — a hearty, layered pasta bake that defines family gatherings and holiday feasts. Unlike Greek Pastitsio or Italian Lasagna, the Egyptian version is distinct for its thick, velvety blankets of sauce and deeply seasoned meat.
steps: Cook the macaroni in salted boiling water until al dente, drain and set aside.
In a pan, sauté onion in oil until golden. Add minced meat and brown thoroughly. Stir in tomato paste, season with salt and pepper. Cook 5 minutes, then set aside.
Melt butter in a saucepan over medium heat. Whisk in flour and cook for 2 minutes until golden. Gradually pour in warm milk, whisking constantly until thickened. Season well.
Remove béchamel from heat and let it cool slightly. Beat in the eggs one at a time.
In a greased deep baking tray, spread half the macaroni. Layer the meat filling evenly. Cover with remaining macaroni.
Pour all the béchamel sauce over the top, spreading to cover completely.
Bake at 180°C (350°F) for 45–50 minutes until the top is deep golden and set.
Let rest for 15 minutes before cutting and serving.

name: Koshari
description: Koshari is Egypt's most famous street food — a high-energy, flavorful carb-fest that brings together an unlikely mix of ingredients into a masterpiece of textures. It's affordable and found on almost every street corner in Cairo.
steps: Boil lentils in water for 20 minutes until just tender. Drain and set aside.
Cook macaroni in salted water until al dente. Drain and set aside.
Toast vermicelli in a dry pan until golden. Add rice and stir. Add water (2:1 ratio), salt, and cook until fluffy.
Deep-fry the sliced onions in batches until deeply crispy and caramelized. Drain on paper towels.
For the tomato sauce: sauté half the garlic in oil, add tomatoes, cumin, salt, and a splash of vinegar. Simmer 15 minutes.
For the garlic vinegar: combine remaining garlic with white vinegar and a pinch of cumin.
To serve, layer rice, lentils, and macaroni in a bowl. Top with chickpeas, crispy onions, tomato sauce, and a drizzle of garlic vinegar.

name: Molokhia
description: Molokhia is perhaps Egypt's most iconic dish, dating back to the Pharaohs. It is a silky jute leaf soup famous for its unique viscous texture and the legendary 'Tasha' — the final sizzle of garlic and coriander poured over the top.
steps: Boil the whole chicken with onion, cardamom, bay leaves, salt and pepper for 45 minutes until cooked through. Reserve the broth.
Bring the chicken broth to a gentle boil. Add the finely chopped molokhia and stir immediately — do not boil hard or it will lose its texture. Simmer 5 minutes.
Prepare the 'Tasha': heat butter and oil in a small pan until very hot. Add all the minced garlic and fry, stirring rapidly, until golden and fragrant (about 30 seconds).
Add the fresh coriander to the garlic pan and stir for 15 seconds.
Pour the sizzling Tasha directly into the molokhia pot. Stir gently. The aroma released is the hallmark of authentic molokhia.
Serve immediately over white rice or with bread, alongside the boiled chicken (roasted or fried).

name: Chicken Ranch Pizza
description: While not a traditional Egyptian dish, Chicken Ranch Pizza has become a massive favourite in modern Egyptian pizzerias. It swaps the traditional red sauce for a creamy, zesty ranch base — a white pizza that is rich, tangy, and incredibly satisfying.
steps: Preheat oven to 230°C (450°F) with a pizza stone or baking sheet inside.
Season sliced chicken with garlic powder, salt, and pepper. Grill or pan-fry until cooked and slightly charred. Set aside.
Roll out pizza dough on a floured surface to your desired thickness.
Spread ranch dressing evenly over the base, leaving a 2cm border.
Scatter half the mozzarella over the ranch sauce. Layer chicken, bell pepper, and onion evenly.
Top with remaining mozzarella and jalapeño if using. Drizzle with olive oil and sprinkle with oregano.
Bake on the hot stone for 12–15 minutes until the crust is golden and the cheese is bubbling and slightly charred.
Rest for 2 minutes, then slice and serve immediately with extra ranch on the side.
